prerequisites: Successful completion of modules to be completed in the 1st and 2nd semesters according to the study plan.

learning_outcomes.text: Students can reproduce the important contents of the relevant standards in the field of operational environmental protection and management and apply them to specific issues.
Students know the important procedures in the field of environmentally integrated production.
They know the position and fields of activity of the company officers for immission, water and radiation protection, as well as for waste management and hazardous substance/goods management.

Students are able to assess and evaluate the necessity of actions in operational process- and product-related environmental protection in specific cases, and to meaningfully select environmentally integrated production methods with regard to wastewater and exhaust air purification, waste treatment, or energy efficiency.

Furthermore, they are able to explain the relevant contexts in exemplary areas of manufacturing-integrated environmental protection (e.g., safety technology, safety management) and to apply the learned methods to corresponding problems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction - Environmental situation. Food and food chain.
Instruments of state control. Development of environmental policy.
Tasks of environmentally integrated production.
Water and Wastewater - Importance of water. Water protection.
Methods for purifying municipal and industrial wastewater.
Air Purity - Structure of the atmosphere. Greenhouse effect.
Flue gas cleaning. Dust separation. Exhaust air cleaning.
Fine dust separation from wood firing systems - Separators and their function.
State of the art.
Filter characterization.
Waste Management - Types of waste and disposal routes. Packaging.
Composting. Landfilling. Thermal recovery.
Hazardous Substances and Safety - Information basis: safety data sheet and operating instructions.
Storage of hazardous substances.
Waste, hazardous goods, and hazardous substance management.
Water and immission protection.
Occupational and plant safety.
Environmental Management Systems according to EMAS and DIN EN ISO 14001 - Design of an environmental policy and implementation of environmental audits.
Definition of an environmental program and the management system in the environmental manual.
Internal audits, management reviews, and certification or validation.
Renewable Energy - Overview, advantages, and disadvantages.
Part 1: Safety Management - Hazard fields and risk perception in societal development.
Legal and other framework conditions.
Protection of the environment.
Organization of plant safety in a company.
Importance of corporate culture.
Occupational safety.
Structural fire protection.
Human factor, knowledge management.
Methodological competence of risk assessment.
Crisis management.
Part 2: Process Engineering Methods for Plant and Process Safety - Methods of risk and hazard analysis.
Safety barriers / inherent safety.
Explosion protection for gases and dusts, electrostatics.
Identification and handling of thermally unstable substances.
Safety of chemical reactions.
Protection with PLT measures.
Protection measure pressure relief.
Assessment of the impact of energy and substance releases.
assessment_rules: The module final examination can be a written exam (180-240 minutes) or an oral exam (45-60 minutes). The award of credit points occurs if the module final examination is passed. In the exam, students should select and fundamentally design for exemplary problems.
